title: Kouroukan Fouga (Manden Charter)
summary: According to Manden tradition, Sundiata Keita proclaimed a set of laws in 1236 at Kouroukan Fouga, near present-day Kangaba in southern Mali, after overthrowing the Sosso ruler Sumanguru Kanté. The charter was spoken, sworn and entrusted to griots rather than written, and UNESCO inscribed it on its intangible heritage list in 2009.

uncertainty.note: Date is traditional; one source says only "early thirteenth century".

as_recorded.value: In 1236, on a clearing of lateritic rock near the town of Ka-ba

where.historical_name: Ka-ba (Kangaba), in the Manden, before the Mali Empire

importance.justification: The charter is a celebrated oral statement of laws and rights in the Manden, recognised by UNESCO as intangible heritage.

sources.title: The Manden Charter: Africa's Constitution Before the Enlightenment
sources.author: Afro Heritage Atlas Team

reviewer_note: The charter was never written down in its original form, so the date is a tradition. The pin is Kangaba Cercle (GeoNames), a district point, with a 25 km uncertainty; one source places the assembly "near the town of Ka-ba". The embassy page says the site is near the Guinean border, which this record does not use.
